units.title: Biomechanical aspects of human movement
units.summary: Biomechanical Aspects of Human Movement Mass The amount of matter of which an object, segment, or body is composed Remain the same regardless of the environment in which the mass exists Centre of Mass (CM) = Centre of Gravity (CG) • CM: an object’s balance point • The body is composed of many parts. Each part can be considered as a single entity, and has a CG • The entire body can be considered as a single mass • S2 • The CG of the typical human body is located in the pelvic region, just anterior to S2 • The CG shifts as the component segments of the body change position or as weight is added or removed from the body Effects of adding/removing weights on shifting the CG

Mass The amount of matter of which an object, segment, or body is composed Remain the same regardless of the environment in which the mass exists
Centre of Mass (CM) = Centre of Gravity (CG) • CM: an object’s balance point • The body is composed of many parts.

units.title: Stability and mobility
units.summary: Stability & Mobility Center of Gravity Base of Support Base of Support (BoS) • BoS • BoS: the contact area of an object with its supporting surface • A largerBoS allows the health worker to accomplish certain tasks with decreased force on the lower back • If the worker’s feet are close together (small BoS), even small weight shifts will move the body’s CG beyond the BoS, requiring the worker bend at the trunk to maintain balance, thus places a great deal of stress on the lower back muscles Mobility Stability is promoted when: • The BoS is greater in area • BoS • The Line of Gravity (LoG) is near the center of BoS • The CG is lower & closer to the BoS Mobility is promoted when: • The BoS is smaller in area • The LoG is allowed to move • BoS beyond the center of the BoS • The distance of CG above the BoS • BoS is greater Remarks: The Line of Gravity (LoG) means the orientation & direction of gravity acting on the full body’s CoM Dynamic Trunk Stabilization • Static stability refers to the property of maintaining and controlling the body’s orientation in space, usually by keeping the LoG within the BoS • In any active human movement, some components of the body are stabilized so that other components can move • The body has to maintain postural control during dynamic activities • The key to achieve postural control is actively contracting the most central muscles of the body, i.e. the core muscles • Dynamic trunk stabilization is maintaining the stability of the trunk and the lumbar spine, within a safe range of movement through activation of core musculature, like transverse abdominis muscles

units.title: Proper body mechanics and force direction
units.summary: Proper Body Mechanics • Body Mechanics: the wayin which we position our bodies during tasks • Because our bodies are subject to the principles of biomechanics • How we position our bodies affects the efficiency of our movements & the stress that is placed on the body tissues • During all patient interaction, the caregiver should position himself using the best body mechanics possible to maximize the ability to accomplish the task with minimal effort in a safe manner • The caregiver assists the client up from the wheelchair, but her upper body bends at the waist with knees straight& trunk angled forward at about 70° • The ES muscle of the trunk must generate sufficient force to maintain the trunk in this flexed position Poor Body Mechanics • The distance between the caregiver and patient decrease, and her knee bent with trunk more upright • The force of ES muscles in this knee-bent & trunk more upright position is lower than the previous straight leg position. • Low back injuries are one of the most common musculoskeletal disorders experienced by people involved in patient mobility tasks. Proper Body Mechanics • In the previous example, we only consider the force exerted on the caregiver’slower back muscles by simply maintaining a flexed trunk position • To complete the transfer task, the caregiver must add the movement of the patient’s body weight into the equation • For optimal performance, both the patient and the caregiver must utilize good body mechanics

• The caregiver assists the client up from the wheelchair, but her upper body bends at the waist with knees straight& trunk angled forward at about 70° • The ES muscle of the trunk must generate sufficient force to maintain the trunk in this flexed position Poor Body Mechanics

• The distance between the caregiver and patient decrease, and her knee bent with trunk more upright • The force of ES muscles in this knee-bent & trunk more upright position is lower than the previous straight leg position.
• Low back injuries are one of the most common musculoskeletal disorders experienced by people involved in patient mobility tasks.
